title: Layout and Packaging
intro: In mixed-signal chips the layout and the package limit speed and precision as much as the schematic does: matching, parasitic coupling, substrate noise and bond-wire inductance all come from here (Razavi, Chapter 19).

blocks.text: Why layout is part of analog design

items: Mismatch from careless placement can far exceed the random mismatch predicted statistically.
Wires add capacitance, resistance, coupling and thermal noise.
Digital circuits on the same die inject noise through the substrate and the shared supplies.
Bond wires and package traces add nanohenries of inductance and picofarads of capacitance that do not scale with the technology.
Design Rules and Multifinger Transistors: what the rules guarantee, the antenna effect, and how to fold wide devices.
Symmetry and Matching: orientation, gate shadowing, dummies, common-centroid layout, trench stress, well proximity and bias distribution.
Passive Device Layout: matched resistors and capacitors, their parasitics and variations, diodes.
Interconnects, Pads and ESD: crosstalk and shielding, wire noise and delay, power buses, pads and electrostatic-discharge protection.
Substrate Coupling: how digital switching reaches analog devices through the substrate, and what to do about it.
Packaging: self- and mutual inductance, supply bounce, decoupling and package resonance.

blocks.caption: Layout cancels process gradients by geometry.

blocks.text: A good habit: whatever you do to one side of a matched pair, do to the other side as well. That applies to wires passing overhead, nearby wells, dummies and the direction of current flow.

blocks.title: Where does the offset come from?
blocks.text: A carefully sized differential pair measures 5 mV of offset, while statistics predict 1 mV. Name three layout causes to check.
solution: Devices placed with different orientations; a gradient across a large pair not cancelled by a common-centroid arrangement; an unrelated wire or a well edge near only one device; unequal routing resistance in the source connections.
